{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Development and Option Agreement

**Prepared for:** Client (AbbVie, as Customer/Licensee)  
**Counterparty:** Harpoon (Vendor/Licensor)  
**Scope:** Playbook review of the filed Development and Option Agreement

---

## 1. Executive summary

The agreement is, on the whole, strongly favourable to us. The indemnity, IP ownership, licence scope, assignment, exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, non-solicitation, MFN, liquidated-damages, renewal and insurance positions all sit at or above our playbook's preferred position, and the termination-for-convenience right in Section 12.3 ("for any or no reason", 90 days' notice, no fee) sits comfortably at our fallback. Several key protections run one-way in our favour — notably the Section 5.8 exclusivity covenant binding Harpoon only, and our unilateral at-will exit — and we do not propose to disturb them.

Three items fail the fallback on material terms and warrant redlines: (i) **limitation of liability** — Section 11.5 excludes consequential damages but contains no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the agreement, leaving unlimited direct-damages exposure; (ii) **audit rights against us** — Section 6.11 permits an audit on mere request with no notice, no business-hours or off-site limitation, no confidentiality obligation on the accounting firm, and with the frequency cap and cost-shifting threshold redacted; and (iii) **post-termination transition** — the exit mechanics oblige us to transfer or destroy data at Harpoon's election with no reciprocal transition assistance or data-return timeline in our favour.

Two procedural caveats. First, the **performance warranty** rule did not complete review and requires manual attention before we go back to the counterparty. Second, our three deviation findings and the warranty finding carry a failed verification flag; the substantive analysis below should be re-confirmed against the execution copy before the redlines are issued.

Finally, this filed copy carries extensive redactions ([\*\*\*]) at several points that matter — the substantive indemnity triggers in Sections 11.1/11.2, the arbitration seat and rules in Schedule 13.7.3, the insurance limits in Section 11.6.1, the default interest rate in Section 6.10, the audit frequency and variance thresholds in Section 6.11, and carve-outs at the end of Section 7.1.2. These are diligence confirmations on the unredacted execution copy, not drafting defects.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 11 INDEMNITY |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 7 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 13.2.2 In the event of [\*\*\*] |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 TERM AND TERMINATION |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | § 12 TERM AND TERMINATION |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (at fallback) | § 13.4.2 [\*\*\*] |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4 COMMERCIALIZATION |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 6.5.3 Reductions. Notwithstanding the foregoing: |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 12 TERM AND TERMINATION |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review** (worker failed; manual review required) | Not identified |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 6.5.3 Reductions. Notwithstanding the foregoing: |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 11 INDEMNITY |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 11 INDEMNITY |
| Low | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 12 TERM AND TERMINATION |

### 2.1 Deviations and proposed redlines

**LOL-CAP — § 11 INDEMNITY (Section 11.5).** Section 11.5 is mutual and delivers the exclusion-of-damages limb (indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, consequential), with carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct and gross negligence, Article 9 confidentiality, Section 5.8 and indemnified Third Party Claims under Article 11. There is no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the agreement, so both parties carry unlimited direct-damages exposure — this fails our fallback's 12-months'-fees cap on a material term. *Proposal:* insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, preserving the existing (A)–(D) carve-outs and adding data protection/security breaches and infringement of the other party's IP as uncapped, with our payment obligations expressly not treated as damages for cap purposes.

**AUDIT — § 6.5.3 (Section 6.11).** The auditor must be independent, of nationally recognised standing and reasonably acceptable to us, and disclosure to Harpoon is limited to correctness and discrepancies — but the audit triggers on mere request with no advance notice, no business-hours or off-site limitation, no confidentiality obligation on the accounting firm (Section 6.13 binds only the Audit Expert), and no bar on direct system access. The frequency cap and cost-shifting variance threshold are redacted, so neither the 12-month cap nor a 5% threshold can be verified. *Proposal:* cap audits at once in any 12-month period on 30 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, conducted off-site where possible, with no direct system access, confidentiality obligations on the auditing firm, and cost-shifting only where the variance exceeds 5%.

**TRANSITION — § 12 TERM AND TERMINATION.** Section 12.6.1(c) requires us to transfer or destroy data at Harpoon's election, while nothing obliges Harpoon to provide post-termination transition assistance or to return our data on a defined timeline. Section 9.7 is request-based, runs only "as soon as reasonably practicable", and sets no export deadline or machine-readable format; the Section 12.10.2 sell-off period gives commercial wind-down but no data or transition support. *Proposal:* insert a new Section 12.6.6 requiring transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Harpoon's then-current rates on expiry or termination, return of our data within 30 days in a standard machine-readable format, and deletion with written certification thereafter. Ninety days of assistance with a 30-day export is an acceptable fallback.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

No walk-away trigger is currently engaged on the findings before us:

- **Joint IP (Section 7.1.2).** Joint IP exists, but each party may Exploit it without consent or accounting, so the joint-ownership walk-away test is not met.
- **Governing law and venue (Section 13.6.1 / 13.7).** Delaware law is an accepted fallback jurisdiction and nothing imposes a foreign forum. **Contingent:** the arbitration seat and rules sit in Schedule 13.7.3, which is redacted. If the seat is outside the United States, the mandatory-arbitration-seated-abroad trigger is engaged and this rule must be re-run as a deviation.
- **Insurance (Section 11.6).** The "no insurance where the vendor processes personal data or works on our premises" trigger is not engaged: this is a compound licence and collaboration with no hosting, data-processing or on-premises work by Harpoon, and Clinical Trial Insurance is folded into the General Liability line.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the three redlines** — the mutual liability cap in Section 11.5, the Section 6.11 audit constraints, and new Section 12.6.6 on transition and data return — as a single consolidated markup.
2. **Complete the WARRANTY review manually.** This rule did not run to completion and no section reference has been identified; we should not send a markup that is silent on performance warranty without confirming the position.
3. **Re-verify before dispatch.** The three deviation findings and the warranty finding carry a failed verification flag; re-confirm the underlying clause text and section references against the execution copy.
4. **Obtain the unredacted execution copy and confirm the redacted terms**, specifically: the Section 11.1/11.2 indemnity triggers (that 11.2 reaches IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law and its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and that our reciprocal 11.1 indemnity is confined to our own development/commercialisation conduct and breach of law); the Schedule 13.7.3 arbitration seat and rules; the Section 11.6.1 insurance limits against the USD 1M/2M benchmark; the Section 6.10 default interest rate; the Section 6.11 audit frequency and variance thresholds; and the carve-outs at the end of Section 7.1.2.
5. **Confirm commercially** the Section 12.6/12.7 reversion mechanics and the Harpoon-set sell-off period under Section 12.10.2, which we have treated as ordinary consequences of a terminated in-licence rather than an exit penalty.
6. **Do not disturb** the provisions running in our favour: the one-way Section 5.8 exclusivity and non-compete on Harpoon, our Section 12.3 at-will termination right, the Section 11.6.3 self-insurance right, the Section 5.9 in-licence first rights, and the Section 12.1.2 conversion of our grants to a fully-paid, royalty-free, irrevocable licence on expiry.
"}
